title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The previous page shows that cochains with coefficients in a sheaf on a simplicial set X_* can be computed as Γ(X_*, C^*_{X_*} ⊗ F). This computes RΓ(X_*, F). Here C^n_* denotes the simplicial k-module [m] ↦ C^n(Δ^m, M).

This page gives the universal property of the cochain complex C^•_{*M}.

(1) Setup. Let A^•_* be a complex of (co)simplicial k-modules, the forms A^n_* in each degree n. Grothendieck writes 'cosimpliciaux', but the variance used is simplicial: there are face maps A_{n+1} → A_n. Concretely, C^n_{*M} : [m] ↦ Map(Hom([n],[m]), M), the n-cochains on Δ^m.

(2) Yoneda step. C^n_{*M} is the right Kan extension (coinduced object) of M from the single object [n]. Hence Hom(A^n_*, C^n_{*M}) ≅ Hom_k(A^n_n, M). A level-wise map u_n corresponds to a single linear map κ_n : A^n_n → M; think of it as 'integration over the standard n-simplex'. Explicitly, a ∈ A^n_m goes to the cochain σ ↦ κ_n(σ^* a).

(3) The two composites. Under this bijection:
- d_C ∘ u_n corresponds to κ_n ∘ ∂_{n+1} : A^n_{n+1} → M, with ∂_{n+1} = Σ(-1)^i d_i the alternating sum of face maps. This is the cochain coboundary, i.e. evaluation on the boundary of Δ^{n+1}.
- u_{n+1} ∘ d_A corresponds to κ_{n+1} ∘ d^n_A : A^n_{n+1} → A^{n+1}_{n+1} → M.

(4) Conclusion (drawn on the next page). Morphisms of complexes A^• → C^•_M are exactly families (κ_n) satisfying the 'Stokes condition' κ_n ∂_{n+1} = κ_{n+1} d_A, i.e. ∫_{∂Δ} ω = ∫_Δ dω.

Purpose: build, for any simplicial set X_*, a map Γ(X_*, A^*_{X_*}) → C^*(X_*, M). It represents RΓ(X_*, A) → RΓ(X_*, M) and is a quasi-isomorphism when A is a resolution of M with κ_0 extending the identity on M. This is an abstract de Rham theorem. It is applied to the simplicial divided-power de Rham complex of the standard simplices over an arbitrary ring k, as an integral substitute for Sullivan's rational polynomial forms.
errors: Variance/terminology: the A^n_* and C^n_{*M} are called 'cosimpliciaux', but the maps used (face maps A_{n+1}→A_n, ∂_{n+1}) and Γ(X_*, ·) for X_* ∈ Δ̂ require simplicial objects. This is a convention slip or a nonstandard naming, not a mathematical error.
Signs are left implicit: ∂_{n+1} must be the alternating sum of face maps for the coboundary correspondence to hold.

ideas.what: Hom of simplicial modules into the simplicial n-cochain module C^n_{*M} ≅ Hom_k(A_n, M) (Yoneda / coinduction)
ideas.modern_name: C^n(Δ^•, M) as the right Kan extension of M along {[n]} ↪ Δ; representability of evaluation at [n]
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Kan; folklore in simplicial homotopy theory)

ideas.what: Chain maps from a simplicial cochain-complex model A^• into simplicial cochains C^•_M correspond to integration maps κ_n : A^n_n → M satisfying the Stokes condition
ideas.modern_name: Integration map / abstract de Rham theorem for simplicial cochain models (Sullivan polynomial forms, Dupont's simplicial de Rham theorem, Cartan's 'théories cohomologiques')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977), H. Cartan (1976), Dupont (1976); integral/divided-power versions by Cenkl–Porter and others

missed.claim: Grothendieck's unpublished 1976 IHÉS treatment frames the comparison of a divided-power de Rham complex with integral cochains over an arbitrary base k through a clean universal property: chain maps into C^•_M are Stokes-compatible families κ_n. This makes it an integral version of the Sullivan/Dupont integration map. The method itself is standard, but the record of Grothendieck working on integral/PD models of cochains in 1975–76 is little known.
missed.quote: et la condition que les u_n définissent bien un hom. de complexes est la "condition de Stokes"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: Grothendieck's work on PD forms as integral cochain models runs alongside Cartan and Sullivan in 1976 and precedes Cenkl–Porter and later integral models. The page itself contains only routine material.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean but standard Yoneda-plus-Stokes argument; its interest is mainly historical, as part of an unpublished integral de Rham theory.
transcription_corrections: Rendering the coboundary composite as κ_n ∂_{n+1} matches the next page's k_n ∂_{n+1}; the maps are κ_n (written k_n on the next page).
The phrase transcribed as '(qui [?] commutent avec d(f) [?])' is illegible and appears to be a parenthetical about compatibility with the simplicial structure; it is uncertain.
The first displayed complex '0 → A^0_* → A^1_* → A^2_* → ⋯' starts with A^0_* (subscript *), consistent with the rest of the page.
